title: Realistic + Investigative: two activity signals to explore
reader_copy: This result places hands-on work with tools, materials, or real-world conditions alongside interest in questions, evidence, and mechanisms. Try the two activities in a small setting and notice whether they support or compete with one another. It does not determine ability, identity, job fit, or a career choice.
tension_prompt: Does the task move naturally from working with something concrete to examining evidence, or do the two activities pull your attention in different directions?
low_risk_experiment: In one short session, alternate a hands-on task with an evidence-checking task; record interest, friction, and the conditions worth exploring next.

title: Realistic + Artistic: two activity signals to explore
reader_copy: This result places hands-on work with tools, materials, or real-world conditions alongside expression through form, style, story, or experience. Use a small task to see whether making and expressing can work together for you. It does not define your personality, skill level, job fit, or career direction.
tension_prompt: When a task needs both a practical result and an expressive choice, which part feels engaging and which part adds friction?
low_risk_experiment: Make a simple physical or practical item, then create one deliberate variation in its form or presentation; note interest, effort, and conditions to check further.

title: Realistic + Social: two activity signals to explore
reader_copy: This result places hands-on work with tools, materials, or real-world conditions alongside supporting, communicating with, or collaborating with people. Keep the two activity signals separate before deciding whether a shared task is appealing. It is not an identity label, an ability conclusion, or a career recommendation.
tension_prompt: Does helping someone around a concrete task add energy, or does the people-facing part change how the practical work feels?
low_risk_experiment: Choose a low-stakes practical task and explain or support one step for another person; record the activity you want to repeat and the conditions that shaped the experience.

title: Realistic + Enterprising: two activity signals to explore
reader_copy: This result places hands-on work with tools, materials, or real-world conditions alongside advancing goals, resources, opportunities, or decisions. Explore the activities as separate signals before treating them as a combined direction. It does not measure leadership, capability, job fit, or future success.
tension_prompt: When practical work needs a goal, resource choice, or decision, do the two parts reinforce each other or compete for attention?
low_risk_experiment: Complete a small practical task and make one bounded choice about its goal, resource, or next step; note interest, strain, and information still missing.

title: Realistic + Conventional: two activity signals to explore
reader_copy: This result places hands-on work with tools, materials, or real-world conditions alongside organizing data, rules, processes, or records. Test whether practical action and structured follow-through fit together in a specific setting. It does not assign a type, prove a skill, or select a career.
tension_prompt: Does structure make a practical task easier to continue, or does the process requirement reduce interest in the hands-on part?
low_risk_experiment: Do one practical task using a short checklist or record sheet; note which actions felt useful, which felt costly, and what context mattered.
